title: Kara-Khitans
capsule: The Kara-Khitai (Western Liao) was a Central Asian empire founded by the Khitan prince Yelü Dashi, who fled westward from the Jurchen Jin dynasty's destruction of the Liao in 1125 and established a new polity centered on Balasagun in the Chu River valley by 1134. At its height the Kara-Khitai controlled the Tarim Basin, Transoxiana, and much of eastern Central Asia, defeating the Seljuk sultan Sanjar at the Battle of Qatwan in 1141 in one of the most decisive Central Asian battles of the medieval period. The state was overthrown from within when the Naiman chief Kuchlug usurped the throne around 1211, and the whole of its territory was absorbed by the expanding Mongol Empire under Jebe by 1218.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is moderately attested through Chinese, Persian, and Syriac sources; the defeat of Sanjar and control of key oasis cities are well documented, but the steppe periphery and degree of effective control over Transoxiana are uncertain, relying on later chronicles and numismatic evidence.
